trajectory_summary: This is an orphaned-system call the rep never formally recognized as such — the customer already owns 11 panels and is doing his own ROI math on expansion, but the rep runs the standard new-lead qualifier script instead of the orphaned_flow. The call never regains energy after the customer's opening objection and ends in a full concession with no appointment and no counter-offer.

observed_outcome.quote: Well, I mean, if anything changes, if you if you're ever open to looking into an estimate, I mean, you know where to call.
observed_outcome.reasoning: Call ends with the rep leaving the door open passively rather than owning any next step; no time, date, or callback was set.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Bill amount ($100-150/month) was captured at 00:53 but never flipped into a reason to act — the customer's very next line reframes it as pool/spa-driven and normal, and the rep does not push back or use the number as leverage; the flip should have landed right after 00:55.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep did not request the actual utility bill or ask the customer to send a bill during the call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: Customer's stated reason for the call (checking if the NM tax credit was still available) is acknowledged factually at 01:25 but never reinforced or used to pivot toward an alternative value proposition (e.g., non-tax-credit purchase options per qualifiers.credit_qualifier notes).

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Missed orphaned_flow trigger on existing-system disclosure
primary_coaching_focus.why: The entire call should have shifted into orphaned-system qualification (installer, ownership type, system working) at this line; instead the rep ran generic new-lead questions and lost the thread of the actual conversation the customer wanted to have.

key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses an existing system, which should trigger the orphaned_flow (ownership type, installer, panel size, system working) — rep never asks any of these.

key_moments.quote: And I don't see there's a financial benefit
key_moments.stewart_read: Classic cost/value objection in the first minute; schema calls for a flip (e.g., reframing the current bill as the real expense) rather than accepting and moving to a qualifier question.

key_moments.stewart_read: Second occurrence of the same ROI objection; rep again does not challenge the math or offer to run a real updated design to verify the 20-year figure.
Third and final concession point — the call ends without any pushback on the stated ROI objection.
